title: FiniteLocalizationPowerColimit
statement: Let A be a commutative ring, iota a finite index type, kappa i a finite type for every i, N i an A-module, and g i t an element of A for each (i,t). Form the sequential diagram of additive groups with constant object the direct sum over i of the products over t of N i, whose successor map sends x_i(t) to g i t times x_i(t). Its colimit is isomorphic to the additive group of the direct sum over i of the products over t of LocalizedModule.Away (g i t) (N i).

source.place: Module localization universal property; perfect.tex lemma-alternating-cech-complex, finite-coordinate colimit calculation (Tag 0911)

proof.text: Apply ModuleCat.localization_away_colimit separately to each coordinate (i,t), obtaining the fraction isomorphism for the power sequence with multiplier g i t.
Forget the coordinate module diagrams to additive groups. Mathlib's forgetful functor preserves filtered colimits, so the coordinate colimits are still the additive groups of the localizations.

Finite products commute with these sequential filtered colimits: move the finitely many representatives to the maximum of their stages for surjectivity; move finitely many coordinate equalities to the maximum of their witness stages for injectivity. Colimits commute with direct sums by the universal property, hence assembling the coordinate isomorphisms yields the displayed isomorphism. Empty coordinate families contribute the zero additive group.

lean.statement:
theorem finiteLocalizationPowerColimit [Finite ι] [∀ i, Finite (κ i)] :
    Nonempty (colimit (finiteLocalizationPowerDiagram A ι κ N g) ≅
      AddCommGrpCat.of (DirectSum ι
        (fun i ↦ ∀ t : κ i, LocalizedModule.Away (g i t) (N i))))
